sources.title: ONNX Runtime Thread Management
verified_facts: The default CPU execution provider exposes explicit intra-op and inter-op thread controls.
Sequential graph execution is the default; parallel graph execution may help branched models but can also hurt performance.
Thread spinning is enabled by default and trades CPU and power use for latency, so its state must be part of an exact runtime manifest.
Graph optimization level is an explicit session option and must be bound to evidence.

sources.title: ONNX Runtime Execution Providers
verified_facts: Execution providers are ordered by priority and determine which graph nodes or subgraphs execute on each provider.
The registered provider list and provider options are observable runtime state.
A portable CPU reference must bind CPUExecutionProvider explicitly and reject an unexpected provider list.

sources.title: ONNX Runtime Graph Optimizations
verified_facts: Graph optimizations have basic, extended, and layout levels and may run online or offline.
Offline optimized artifacts must use the same execution-provider, optimization, and target-hardware assumptions as their eventual runtime.
An offline optimized graph is a separate derived artifact and is not implied by the source ONNX model.

sources.title: Install ONNX Runtime
verified_facts: The official CPU Python distribution is the onnxruntime package.
Windows builds have explicit runtime prerequisites, so lock metadata alone does not prove an installed or loadable environment.
